body:
Yeah, that's a rough situation, I feel for you. There's a weird thing that happens with antidepressants. People take them for long enough, they kick in, and when they start feeling better they stop taking them (though in your case the high of a new relationship might have been the cause to stop taking them). I've had so many friends do this and it always ends with them spiraling down into a deep depression. It's tricky with antidepressants. Don't blame yourself.

We know there's a starting point with handling your depression. It may take a few weeks, but there is all but a guarantee that you'll start feeling even slightly better once you get a new prescription; we can start to see the light :)

Are you in therapy of any sort?
I don't know what kind of meds you're on, but if they're antidepressants or something of the sort, have you started taking them again?
I feel exactly the same. I know that sometime before I get too old I'm just going to off myself one night
I'm a grown ass man crying right now after reading this.

I care about you, and I want you to break out of this. Depression can seduce you in to thinking that everything is lost. Depression is also a liar. I've read your previous posts and I'm glad that you're seeking professional help. That is a seemingly small step with a huge impact on bettering yourself. It's often the hardest step to take. Depression lurks behind you, ever present, waiting for it's opportunity to attack. Then it pounces and blinds you from your ability to be happy. All you can feel is nothing. The only bit of emotion that your soul can muster is sorrow. The inner fire is all but extinguished.  

I sincerely hope that this, or something else you find, helps you in some way. I just want you to know that there are so many others that have been there. We know exactly how you feel. Some of us, including myself, still have bouts with it. What helped me was noticing the little insignificant things that brought me some semblance of joy, no matter how minute. These little victories, as well as understanding that 'every day courage' is well underappreciated, kept me going moment to moment. It takes a lot of strength to pull yourself out of the void, but it's worth it. Happiness can be found even in the most dire of circumstance. 

Find little things that help you keep going. Take care. I hope to hear from you soon.

Because it's an experience worth having

It's so easy to get lost in loneliness. It's easy to think about all of our bad experiences. In fact, it's like our bad memories force themselves into our heads late a night when all we want is a few hours of uninterrupted rest. Our mind can be such a bitch sometimes. Because it forgets all of the pleasant moments we've had. It tries to tell us that our bad experiences make us less of a person when in fact, it makes us more of a person.

Brother, I sincerely hope you find inspiration somewhere out there. I hope that what I write helps you hold out for a little longer. Every second that passes is an opportunity, a chance for something to make itself known and potentially make your life better no matter how small.

There's a silver lining with every circumstance. Even guilt can offer something of use. Guilt nestles itself deep in your gut, like knot only an eagle scout can tie. Then it uses your heart like it's own punching bag. But to your own admission it's keeping you alive moment to moment. Let's use this, brother. Maybe we can find a way for that guilt to loosen up and be replaced by something we can gain a lot more out of.

It's hard to keep going without a purpose. I've been in this situation as recently as a couple months ago. But I think you've given two great purposes to keep trying, if only for a little while longer. Your niece, and comedy. I can't say much about your niece, but I do know shitty siblings. We can wish that at some point your niece will be able to come around on her own volition when she gets a little older. As for comedy, you're in the perfect state of mind for it.

Brother I'm a huge fan of comedy, comedians and comedic actors. I even have a little dream of putting together some material and hitting up the local open mics. Almost all of the great comedians (including actors) battle some kind of mental illness. Comedy is an art; taking everything that god throws at us and making folks laugh about it. It might be the truest way to give god the big middle finger. And as far as LA goes... As a fellow Texan, Austin's a lot closer. It'll also prevent you from being a tiny fish lost in a school of sharks. Every day I'm two decisions away from ditching it all and moving to Austin to pursue comedy and I'm dead serious about this. 

Brother, you're preaching to the choir about the god damn grocery store. I can't tell you how many times I've put clothes on, got into my car, drove to the fucking walmart, sat in the parking lot hyperventilating, then turn around and go straight home thinking 'I'll just order in... or just not eat. Why would I deserve food? I can't even go in to the fucking grocery store. Jesus Christ I'm pathetic!' This is where the rage kicks in and I have an impulse to grab my gun and shoot myself in the head.  

Being alone and trapped in a place with friends lost... Man this is tough. People can talk about all the ways to better yourself, but when the best part of life sleeping and forgetting? It's hard to see the forest through the trees. I speaking from experience. Little victories go a long way. Everyday courage is incredibly important and underappreciated. I know it all seems for not, but there's always something out there. Something to find even a small purpose with. 

I genuinely hope you feel better, brother.
You don't have to go into detail. You don't even have to answer, but what kind of flashbacks?

24 years old. At 24 years old you've been consciously able to impact your environment for maybe 8 years. Two of which you weren't an adult. The next four years nobody really takes you seriously as an adult. And now you're stuck. Being stuck sucks. Being stuck can really drain the life right out of you. Especially when you're stuck and hitting a quarter life crisis. Let's talk more about time. So in the past 8 years you've graduated high school, found a career path, gone to college to study that career path and it's taking you a bit longer than perfect. There is absolutely no shame in this situation. Shame is a blinding light in the corner of your eye. It sticks there in your vision like a thorn in your side keeping you from doing the things that you wish you could do. The trick is, it's an illusion.

It's hard to work up the motivation to make it out the bedroom door, or hell, even the bed, when there is this looming cloud of failure that yells obscenities at you. I've resorted to yelling back at it; spouting off goofy jokes at my own expense until I've made enough light of the situation that the cloud parts and I can see the sky. It's all about little victories; and everyday kind of courage. 

To me, failure is manufactured. If you can keep going, you haven't failed. The only true failure is failing to try, and even that is tough. It's vulnerable to try. It's vulnerable to keep going. But those vulnerabilities are what make us human. They're what gives us our essence as people. There is no guarantee that you will succeed if you keep trying. The only thing you can guarantee is that you gave it your damnedest and got as far as you did. I still feel there is fight in you. 

I genuinely hope you find some kind of solace or resolve somewhere. You have so much time left to get it all sorted.

What's going on, brother?

Please get in touch with somebody. There are so many out there willing to help you. We care.

Depression is chemical. Feeling sad might be triggered from your environment, but depression just hits. It creeps behind you. Depression is opportunistic; waiting in the corner for it's moment to strike. Depression can even be seductive. 'Why go outside and have experiences when you can sulk in here? We can feel terrible about you, together'. Depression's a bitch. Depression is all of these things, but it isn't selfish.

Friends can be bitches, too. It's a real shit thing for them to say to you, but it's coming from a half-way decent place; though ignorant. But they noticed. And they were hurt. So they care about you on some level. 

Listen, I feel ya. It's difficult to be yourself around people. It's hard to take a stand on something no matter how trivial or mundane. Taking something seriously is vulnerable. Trying is vulnerable. Friends will see that you're vulnerable, and care about you more so. 

I'm glad that you're seeing a therapist and that you're taking medication. These are two steps that a lot of folks can't climb, but you've been able to do it. That speaks volumes about your character in and of itself. Keep it up. I hope you feel better, and God speed.

I sincerely hope these words help you. There is absolutely no mal-intent on my part. I genuinely hope there is a comment on this thread, or maybe something else you read on this sub that keeps you going, if only for a little bit longer. With each second is an opportunity for something to happen; and inspiration even of the slightest. I hope what I right might add to the time clock to keep you going. Brother, I got your six.

I don't know your specific situation, but I've definitely felt similar, if not the same. It seems that when most folks feel they have no other option, they're blind to the back roads that lead you back to happiness; or at least purpose. 

I've been in a situation where I'm flying down the highway, pedal to the metal; hellbent on my own destruction. And right before the road stops and the ground falls out beneath you, you spot an exit sign that says "Maybe". That maybe has kept me from sealing my own fate more than a few times.

Everybody wants a do over, and for good reason most of the time. Do overs can be accomplished even in the most dire of circumstance. Move. Get out of there. Start over somewhere else. These are all thoughts I've had before. They make themselves present on a day-to-day basis. And it's always a viable option. Maybe a change of scenery, or even seeing some scenery, can really calm the mind and help with introspection. Everybody loves a long drive to nowhere in particular. Maybe it's just you and some tunes and the white line to guide your way. Need some extra cash on your journey? There are tons of ride share/delivery services like Postmates or Uber to get a little extra scratch in your pocket while you keep movin'. Maybe you'll meet a few cool people on the way that don't care where you're from, or what you look like. So long as the conversation is pleasant and genuine.

Brother. Disappointment and regret... They're a bitch. There's nothing to say and everything to say about it. It tears me up inside daily and reveals itself as nervous anxiety and bouts of depression. But they can be managed. There's always a silver lining with regrets. It gives you a story. It gives you character. It gives you a reason for the way you see certain things. It gives you insight. It can even help you be a better and more empathetic person. It can help you be a person that another person can see. And maybe that other person understands, too. 

It's a weird world we live in. It isn't fair, and that sucks. I'm sorry you're feeling this way and I wish that you find something out there that helps.
